about: Project Story S2: what the game said before its conversations moved into scripts, recorded in the real game (?fixture=town, headless) with talkLine, startTrainer and healAll swapped for recorders, on main at 509c990: personTalk (each person, visit after visit), trainerTalk (first meeting, met, beaten; a trainer with intro lines runs rivalScene), talkHazel (Index 1/6/20, badges 0/1/3, Blake beaten on the golf course or not, the player named Rae), storyAfterRival (win, lose, skipped) and storyEnding. tools/test/story-snapshot.test.mjs plays the scripts against it. RL-5 (owner’s answer): the lines that sent you to the parked places were cut from Hazel’s, Granny Juniper’s and the townsfolk’s talk; their records here lost the same lines and nothing else. Redone on 2026-10-23 from the scripts for the owner’s new professor: hazel, after-rival and ending say the Chosen’s approved lines; person:hazel_lab (Hazel in the lab, his assistant) is new.

person:juniper.text: There you are, dear. Up and about already? You came down in my lavender. Flattened half of it.
Hazel looked you over and says you’ll live. I’ve made up the little room in my cottage. It’s yours for as long as you want it.
Come in whenever you like. Have a rest, and your Billies will feel better for it too.
Honey’s in the jar by the door. Don’t tell the bees I said so.
Hazel works too hard. Take her some honey if you’re passing the lab.
The wind sail turns all day and keeps the lanterns lit all night. Copper, sun and a bit of wind: that’s all a village needs.
Things fall into Copperleaf every week or so. Mostly furniture. You’re the first one I’ve kept.
You’ve been walking! I can tell. You’ve got that Hollow Earth colour in your cheeks.
The bees know everyone in Copperleaf. They’ll get used to you.
Honey’s in the jar by the door. Don’t tell the bees I said so.

person:nacre.text: You came down the lift? Then you’ve seen the pipes. Everyone up there thinks they carry water.
They carry gold. Ours. Vinylla’s pressing plant has been pumping the city’s vaults dry for a year to pay for her tour.
The ledger is in the Exchange, if you can stomach the numbers. Somebody ought to send her the bill.
We sank because we wouldn’t spend. Now someone else is spending it for us. There’s a lesson in that, but I’m too cross to learn it.
The bubble trams run all night. There is no night down here, only the lamps.
Mind your coins on the lift. Things that fall in the trench stay in the trench.
The mirrors bring the Inner Sun down to us. Nobody can own the sun, not even in Pearlantis. Especially not in Pearlantis.
We sank because we wouldn’t spend. Now someone else is spending it for us. There’s a lesson in that, but I’m too cross to learn it.

trainer:chad.text: I’ve been training out here all morning. Mine knows a lot more than Tackle now.
What happened outside the lab doesn’t count. This one counts.
Nobody plays through this course until we settle it. Let’s go!
Hey! I’ve been waiting for you.
I picked the starter that beats yours. Let’s see what you’ve got.

trainer:crude.text: Welcome to the Fizzwell arena. Here we battle in a sandstorm.

trainer:markdown.text: Welcome to the Lanternhall arena. Polished floors, polished team.
Every Steel Billie on my team makes the others hit harder.

trainer:chad2.text: There you are! I’ve been training on the farm all week.
My starter evolved. Did yours? Doesn’t matter. I’m winning this time.

trainer:intern.text: I’m only here for the experience. And the battles.

trainer:alta.text: Welcome to the top. The air is thin and so is my patience.
My Flying team has never once looked down.

My Water team flows around every attack.

trainer:geo.text: Careful, the ground is literally melting.
I study volcanoes. Mostly I study running away.

trainer:poppy.text: Everything here grows back twice as fast. Including my temper, since the merch stalls arrived.
Let’s see if your team blooms under pressure.

trainer:variant_fest2.text: Low number, see? I was a fan before it was limited.

trainer:gardener.text: I sweep the petals every morning. They fall again by lunch. I think that’s the job.

trainer:vault.text: Welcome to Goldvine Town. Everything you can see is mine, and everything you can’t see is in a vault, and also mine.
I rented the vaults to a pop star. And myself, as it turns out. Read the small print, child.

trainer:variant_vault.text: These vaults are full of variants. Vinyl ones. Of the same record. You wouldn’t understand.

trainer:sommelier.text: Notes of oak, leather and a very aggressive pricing strategy.

trainer:accountant.text: Flat tax! Everyone pays the same. I have a form explaining why that’s fair. It’s very long.

trainer:prospector.text: Struck gold in ’98. Struck it again in ’99. It was the same gold. I keep losing it.

trainer:morel.text: The forest remembers every spore. The Variants are grinding up its memory to make a record shine.

trainer:variant_spore.text: Every spore we grind makes the record shine a little brighter. The forest doesn’t mind. We asked it. It didn’t answer.

trainer:forager.text: Never eat a mushroom you can’t afford. Most of these cost more than you.

trainer:peeper.text: The leaves turn every quarter. I’ve been here forty quarters. I am leaving next quarter.

trainer:founder.text: We’re pre-revenue. Pre-product. Pre-office, now the jungle has it. But the vision is huge.

trainer:carat.text: The Variants want one perfect needle, long enough to play the sun. I’m cutting it. I didn’t ask what for.
I’m asking now. Show me what you’re made of.

trainer:variant_needle.text: The needle has to be perfect. One scratch and the sun skips.

trainer:geologist.text: These crystals grew a millimetre a century. The Variants are cutting a metre a day.

trainer:spelunker.text: Don’t look into the pool too long. It looks back, and it’s doing your accounts.

trainer:icefisher.text: I fish for coins through the ice. The safe is frozen solid, but sometimes the interest leaks out.

trainer:sailor.text: See that shell? Four hundred companies live in it. None of them have ever been seen.

trainer:yachtbroker.text: Every yacht in this harbour has a smaller yacht, to get to the bigger yacht. I sell the smallest ones.

trainer:variant_press.text: Lucky number! I got to stand by the press. I can feel it in my teeth.

trainer:cass.text: Stop right there. This is a closed set.
Wait. You? We dropped you. Down a hole. On the surface.
You were the best sound engineer the tour ever had. Then you read the plans.
It doesn’t matter. The press is nearly done, and you’re not on the guest list.
Nothing personal. It’s just the bottom line.

trainer:sysadmin.text: Have you tried turning the Cloud off and on again? I have. It rained for a week.
Have you tried turning the Cloud off and on again? I have. It rained for a week.

trainer:chad3.text: There you are. Took you long enough.
Vinylla’s people offered to buy my team. All of it. Dad’s clone too, for the collection.
I said no. I think I said no. I’m not used to saying it.
Battle me. If I can still beat you, I meant it.
For the record: this isn’t for sale.

trainer:vip.text: VIP means Very Important Purchaser. I have every variant. Even the ones that don’t exist yet.
VIP means Very Important Purchaser. I have every variant. Even the ones that don’t exist yet.

trainer:mascot.text: I was Bubbles the Bubble for nine years. They never told me it burst. I found out from the newspaper.
I was Bubbles the Bubble for nine years. They never told me it burst. I found out from the newspaper.

trainer:variant_vip2.text: Number one. The first fan. I was here before the tower. I watched them build it round me.

trainer:vinylla1.text: Oh! The sound engineer. Cass said you’d bounced. I love a comeback; they chart so well.
You know what I’m pressing. A lid for the sun, gold on one side. Light, by subscription.
People pay for scarcity. I’m making the scarcest thing there is.
Let’s do a little soundcheck, darling.
Every limited edition needs a launch.

trainer:daytrader.text: I bought at the all-time high. I’m waiting for it to come back. It’s been eleven years.
I bought at the all-time high. I’m waiting for it to come back. It’s been eleven years.

trainer:bellringer.text: I ring the bell when the day is done. The sun never sets here, so I just ring it when I’m tired.
I ring the bell when the day is done. The sun never sets here, so I just ring it when I’m tired.

trainer:variant_one.text: Number one. Not the first fan; the first variant. She made me before she made the record.

trainer:vinylla2.text: You came all this way for the release? I’m touched. Truly.
One turn of the press and the sun is a record. Gold on one side, darkness on the other.
And every one of them will pay to listen.
This is the last track, darling. Make it count.

trainer:deepdiver.text: I’ve dived for the bottom line twenty times. It keeps moving down.

trainer:tinker.text: Built them myself. Want to see what they can do?

after-rival:win.text: What? I lost to someone who fell out of the sky an hour ago?
Mine only knows Tackle. That’s my excuse and I’m sticking to it.
I’m off to train on the golf course. Next time I’ll have a whole team. Try to keep up!
There. Good as new. I have healing hands. Hazel has a first-aid kit. Same thing.
Granny Juniper made up a room for you in her cottage, by the hives. Every hero needs a base.
Now go and explore! The road teaches more than any book. I’ve read zero books, and look at me.

ending:vinylla2.text: Gold. Everywhere. On the floor, on the press, on the record...
Aurumansa. The golden caravan. I foresaw this. I didn’t write it down, but I foresaw it.
Look at it, Vinylla. Gold all over the pressing floor. Nothing here is limited any more.
Do you know what a record is worth if everyone can have one?
About what it’s worth to listen to it. Turns out that was the point.
And you. You were the sound engineer on her tour. You read the plans, and Cass made sure you fell.
Welcome back. The sun is still up. It will be up tomorrow too.

person:hazel_lab.text: Oh, you’re back. In one piece, too. That never stops being surprising.
People don’t fall through the crust and live. You did, and you can still talk. I’m writing a paper about it.
He isn’t a professor. He isn’t technically anything. But the Billies like him, so here we are.
If he gives you a type tip, do the opposite. It works more often than you’d think.
The katana has been at the cleaners for two years. Don’t ask.
Granny Juniper sends honey. I hide it from him. You didn’t see that.
Oh, you’re back. In one piece, too. That never stops being surprising.
